plan.title: [framework-gap] Deposited 5-second SessionStart hook timeout is routinely exceeded on Windows (4.9s-6.5s measured on agy 1.5.18)

narratives.Description: Raise the deposited SessionStart hook timeout from 5 to 30 seconds for every host (Claude, Grok, Codex, agy, Cursor), matching the deposited tool.before timeout. On Windows, agy SessionStart runs measured 4.9s-6.5s, so half of them were killed before injecting the notice.
narratives.Overview:
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The deposited SessionStart hook timeout for every host (Claude, Grok, Codex, agy via `NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, and Cursor via `CURSOR_SESSION_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) is 30 seconds, matching the deposited `tool.before` timeout.
- [ ] Each timeout is its own named constant, not a reused literal.
- [ ] Repair treats a deposit carrying the old 5-second SessionStart timeout as drift and rewrites it.
- [ ] Tests assert the SessionStart timeout in each host's deposited entry.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows operator with a deposited host hook, I want SessionStart to have enough time to finish so that the session notice and applying-host record are not silently dropped.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Add a named SessionStart timeout constant per host family in init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts (nested hosts and Cursor), set both to 30, and use them in the deposit, drift check and coverage-applicability evaluator. Old 5-second deposits then fail the equality check and repair rewrites them. Update the tests that pin the 5-second value.
narratives.Traces: clause.1 -> agent-hooks.ts constants; clause.2 -> distinct named constants; clause.3 -> hasRegistration drift checks; clause.4 -> agent-hooks.test.ts and evaluate.test.ts

issueCommentThread.body:
Rewriting the body to criteria-only for ingest; added to the 0.132.1 maintainer release (Scott, yolo overnight). No arc: the fix and files are named. Prior body quoted below.

<details><summary>Prior body</summary>

## Summary

Deposited 5-second SessionStart hook timeout is routinely exceeded on Windows (4.9s-6.5s measured on agy 1.5.18)

## Context

Directive 0.132.0 on Windows (win32) with live Antigravity (agy 1.5.18) hooks active (internal benchmark evidence (private)). Measuring wall-clock runtime of the deposited SessionStart hook command (node .agents/deft-hook-*.mjs --host agy --event session.start) across four consecutive warm runs.

## Expected behavior

The deposited SessionStart hook timeout provides enough headroom on Windows for outer node + git rev-parse + inner hook-bin.js + SessionStart bookkeeping to complete reliably, inject the SessionStart notice, and publish .deft/applying-host.json.

## Actual behavior / gap

init-deposit/agent-hooks.js hardcodes timeout: 5 seconds for SessionStart across hosts (NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5 for Claude/Grok/Codex/AGY; CURSOR_SESSION_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5 for Cursor), whereas tool.before was already raised to 30 seconds. Four consecutive warm runs of the AGY SessionStart hook on Windows measured 4913 ms, 4920 ms, 6448 ms, and 5008 ms -- half of all runs exceeded the 5-second timeout and would be killed by the host before injecting the notice or completing SessionStart bookkeeping.

## Session notes

Observed on win32 with Node v24.18.0 and agy 1.5.18 under the flat SessionStart schema (Refs #7440, #7347, #7416). Raising the deposited SessionStart timeout (e.g. to 15-30s on parity with tool.before) or trimming subprocess spawns in the SessionStart path prevents silent SessionStart drops on Windows. Source: internal benchmark evidence (private).

---
_Filed via `deft feedback:file` from a directive consumer project (Refs #1709 value-feedback gap escalation)._



</details>

expected_outputs: deposited SessionStart timeout is 30 seconds for every host; old 5-second deposits repair as drift
